headline.purpose: Operational page headings; the oversized sign-in slogan is not a reusable display role.

headline-mobile.purpose: Page headings at widths up to 760px.

title-mobile.purpose: Major work sections at widths up to 760px.

objective.purpose: Fluid task meaning; later CSS supersedes the former desktop/mobile fixed sizes.

label.purpose: Button text; ordinary form labels inherit their surrounding line height.

navigation.purpose: Project and conversation navigation; current items increase to weight 600.

input.purpose: Native field text; weight follows its surrounding control or label.

workflow-title.purpose: Titles inside workflow documents and plan surfaces.

context-title.purpose: Alignment, latest observation and compact definition headings.

outcome.purpose: Semantic task result title, separate from the current step and assessment text.

guide-introduction.purpose: Guide introduction at regular body weight and line height.

detail.purpose: Step explanations, alignment messages and supporting workflow prose.

reading.purpose: Task freshness, agreement notes and links.

breadcrumb.purpose: Quiet linked project scope above the single conversation navigation row.

assessment-label.purpose: Bold Supervisor assessment label inside the step explanation.

step-state.purpose: Compact textual journey status; color is supplementary.

motion.name: control-border
motion.purpose: Buttons and links only when reduced motion is not requested; no lift or entrance animation.

motion.name: journey-marker-state
motion.purpose: Journey markers only when reduced motion is not requested; no pulse, lift or automatic progress animation.

breakpoints.name: workflow-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Named workflow inline-size container; plan stacks and context becomes two columns.

breakpoints.name: workflow-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Named workflow inline-size container; context and step metadata stack.

breakpoints.name: negotiation-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Named negotiation inline-size container; plan/alignment stack and sticky alignment becomes static.

narrative.overview:
Transport interchange wayfinding gives Supervisor a stable midnight-indigo navigation field and clear work surfaces. Teal marks the selected route; action blue identifies links, controls and keyboard focus. The personality comes from aligned information, restrained geometry and readable operational type.

The workspace is compact without compressing the meaning of work. A task statement, semantic outcome, connected workflow and actual plan alignment each have a distinct reading role. Native activity, Supervisor assessment and agreement remain separate facts. Borders and tonal insets organize detail; narrow containers stack the same content and follow the system color preference. This is an extension of the existing Operate system, with the existing application mark and source assets unchanged.

This record is extracted from the current local UI source, with retained fixture captures as supporting visual evidence. The surface direction contract owns the page strategy and online pattern references. No new visual-world seed was rolled for this extension; the inherited seed is not verified provenance, and no approved raster comp or new raster is involved. Shared review paths can be overwritten by later recaptures; this document does not establish their freshness, installed behavior or deployment status.
keyCharacteristics: A persistent indigo navigation field beside a quiet work canvas.
Aligned rows and explicit text labels for state, scope and freshness.
Connected, collapsible workflow branches with a named current step.
A separate agreement region and clearly disclosed retained history.
Blue actions, teal selection and semantic amber/red attention.
Flat bordered surfaces, modest corners and minimal motion.

rules.name: The Accent Roles Rule
rules.body: Use action blue for links, controls and work-area focus. Use teal for selected project routes and conversation views; the indigo rail keeps its own selected fill and pale-teal icon.

rules.name: The State Needs Words Rule
rules.body: Pair every status color or activity dot with text. Amber and red describe an actual issue, state or explicit disable action; native activity remains separate from supervision and assessment.

rules.name: The Operational Type Rule
rules.body: Use the platform sans for work content, labels and operational headings. Reserve monospace for source, paths and identifiers; status labels stay in sentence case.

rules.name: The Single Boundary Rule
rules.body: Give a work surface one quiet border. Inside an existing panel, separate sections with rules and spacing instead of another rounded card.

rules.name: The Topology Before Totals Rule
rules.body: Preserve sequence, parallel and nested workflow boundaries, and keep parent assessment independent from child completion.

rules.name: The Current Task Rule
rules.body: Bind current outcome and alignment to the selected task; retain unrelated workflow records as explicitly labeled history without presenting their agreement as the current task's agreement.

dos: Do preserve the indigo navigation field and the distinction between canvas, work surface and tonal inset in both color schemes.
Do keep state labels, native activity, read times and uncertainty readable together.
Do preserve full workflow topology, explicit proposal/agreed/historical contexts and the distinction between current-task alignment and retained history.
Do lead with task meaning and a named semantic outcome before exposing provenance.
Do use visible keyboard focus, labeled controls and the existing narrow-screen reflow.
Do draw icons as consistent stroked SVG and keep monospace for literal technical content.
donts: Don't use amber or red as decoration, or let a color alone communicate status.
Don't add decorative shadows, gradients or nested rounded cards to the flat work surfaces.
Don't infer completed work from an accepted plan, a completed child, quiet native activity or an assessed-step count.
Don't repeat project navigation inside the conversation navigation or expose checkout selection outside Definitions.
Don't reuse the sign-in display scale for workspace labels.
